_doc: Hand-curated scoring inputs for Stage 4 (scripts/track2/s4_rank.py). c1 (max 25) and c3 (max 15) are lists of evidence items, each worth points with a source, so leave-one-source-out can remove them. c2 (max 20) is scored per mechanism scenario M1-M4. c4 (max 15), c5 (max 15) and c6 (max 10) are single judgements, each with a reason. gate: pass | review | exclude. Scores are judgements, documented so they can be challenged; they are not measurements.

candidates.status: Approved Rx (FDA/EMA, extended-release for dyslipidaemia); also OTC

c1.note: NAD+ precursor NMN raises BubR1 abundance in vivo; NAD+ decline drives BubR1 loss via SIRT2/K668
SIRT2 overexpression extends median lifespan of BubR1 H/H mice (genetic, same axis)

c2.why: All patient BUBR1 is p.N1002K (allele 1 is null), so raising abundance only helps if the stabilised mutant protein works. Fits best under M1

c3.note: Healthspan and lifespan of BubR1 H/H improved via SIRT2
Niacin raises blood NAD+ up to 8x and restores muscle NAD+ in humans (mitochondrial myopathy)

c4.why: Decades of use; paediatric dyslipidaemia experience; flushing, hepatotoxicity (SR forms), glucose intolerance

c5.why: Raises uric acid (stone risk with nephrocalcinosis needs monitoring); raising NAD+ may support tumour metabolism (NAMPT is pro-tumour in some cancers), and there are no RMS data

c6.why: Oral, cheap; testable in patient lymphocytes or fibroblasts with NAD+ and BUBR1 western blot readouts

candidates.counter: Wu 2023 (38009412): SIRT2 overexpression does not extend lifespan in wild-type mice, so the benefit may be specific to low-BubR1 states (which applies here). The niacin -> BUBR1 link is not tested directly. Nicotinamide, NR and NMN are supplements, not approved drugs.
candidates.hypothesis: Niacin or NAD+ repletion raises steady-state BUBR1-N1002K and lowers PCS and missegregation in patient cells
candidates.endpoint: BUBR1 western blot (vs cycloheximide chase), K668 acetylation, PCS rate, live-cell mitotic timing

candidates.node: Chaperone capacity (HSF1/HSP70 co-inducer) -> BUBR1 fold stability

c1.note: Kinase-domain MVA mutants depend on HSP90 for stability; arimoclomol itself is untested on BUBR1 and acts mainly on HSP70

c2.why: A pharmacological chaperone-network approach for a destabilised fold. Requires the mutant to be a chaperone client (shown for analogous MVA alleles)

c3.note: Restores folding or trafficking of misfolded proteins in other diseases

c4.why: Approved from age 2; mostly mild adverse effects (URTI, diarrhoea, weight loss); hypersensitivity warning

c5.why: Raises serum creatinine 10-20% via OCT2 (confounds kidney monitoring with nephrocalcinosis); HSF1 activation is pro-tumorigenic in some models

c6.why: Can be tested in vitro alongside an HSP90-dependence assay; costly

candidates.counter: No evidence links HSP70 induction to BUBR1. Boosting chaperones could help tumour cells too.
candidates.hypothesis: Arimoclomol increases BUBR1-N1002K half-life in patient cells in an HSF1-dependent manner
candidates.endpoint: Cycloheximide-chase half-life with or without drug; HSP70 induction; PCS rate

c2.why: Non-specific chemical chaperone; it is also an HDAC inhibitor, which could change BubR1 acetylation either way

c4.why: Long paediatric use in urea cycle disorders; high sodium load, body odour, menstrual effects

c5.why: No clear tumour signal; sodium load matters for kidney and blood pressure

candidates.counter: No BUBR1 data at all. HDAC-inhibitor effects on mitosis are a confounder.
candidates.hypothesis: 4-PBA raises BUBR1-N1002K abundance without changing K668 acetylation

candidates.node: mTORC1 hyperactivity -> sarcopenia; senescence and SASP

c1.note: Sarcopenia in monoallelic BubR1 MVA-mutant mice correlates with mTORC1 hyperactivity (correlation, no drug tested)

c2.why: Acts downstream, so it is largely independent of the variant mechanism

c3.note: mTORC1 is linked to an MVA-relevant tissue phenotype
Rapamycin extends healthspan in other mouse ageing models (not BubR1)

c4.why: Everolimus approved from age 1 (TSC); immunosuppression, mucositis, impaired wound healing, dyslipidaemia, growth concerns

c5.why: Temsirolimus with VAC/VI was feasible in RMS (ARST1431) but gave no EFS benefit; activity in relapsed RMS (ARST0921). Proteinuria needs monitoring

c6.why: Oral; S6K phosphorylation readout; in vitro and in patient muscle cells

candidates.counter: mTOR inhibition induces autophagy, and autophagy degrades BubR1 in senescent cells (37094517), so it might lower BUBR1 further. Immunosuppression during cancer therapy.
candidates.hypothesis: Low-dose rapalog lowers SASP and senescence in patient fibroblasts without lowering BUBR1 or raising missegregation
candidates.endpoint: pS6, SA-beta-gal, SASP panel, BUBR1 level, karyotype

candidates.status: Dasatinib approved (paediatric Ph+ ALL/CML); quercetin is a supplement

c1.note: Genetic clearance of p16+ cells in BubR1 H/H delays progeroid phenotypes (not a drug)
D+Q lowered senescence markers in BubR1 H/H fat (patent data, not peer-reviewed)

c2.why: Mechanism-independent; targets consequences, not the defect

c3.note: Healthspan (fat, muscle, eye) improved; no lifespan extension

c4.why: Paediatric oncology use; myelosuppression, pleural effusion, QT; intermittent senolytic dosing is untested in children

c5.why: Senescence is a tumour barrier in a cancer-predisposed child; overlaps with chemotherapy myelosuppression. ChEMBL: no BUBR1 inhibition (>75% residual activity at 1 uM)

c6.why: In vitro senolysis of patient fibroblasts is straightforward

candidates.counter: Healthspan but not lifespan benefit; it does not address the tumour risk and might remove a tumour-suppressive barrier.
candidates.hypothesis: D(+Q) selectively removes senescent patient fibroblasts without enriching aneuploid proliferating cells
candidates.endpoint: SA-beta-gal/p16 clearance; interphase FISH aneuploidy of survivors

candidates.branch: A/B: block autophagic BUBR1 loss; aneuploidy-selective

c1.note: Autophagy-dependent BubR1 degradation in senescent cells (oxidative-stress model, not MVA)

c2.why: Two arms: preserves BUBR1 from autophagy (but proteasome is the route shown for MVA mutants), and is selectively toxic to aneuploid cells

c3.note: Chloroquine is aneuploidy-selective in trisomic MEFs

c4.why: Long paediatric use; retinal toxicity with long-term use; QT

c5.why: Autophagy inhibition is under clinical study as an anticancer approach (paediatric data limited); dose adjustment in renal impairment

c6.why: Cheap; in vitro LC3 flux and BUBR1 readouts

candidates.counter: MVA mutant BUBR1 is cleared by the proteasome, not shown to go through autophagy. Killing aneuploid cells in a mosaic child could harm tissues, an untested risk.
candidates.hypothesis: HCQ raises BUBR1 in patient cells under stress and preferentially reduces aneuploid-cell fitness
candidates.endpoint: LC3-II flux, BUBR1 level, FISH aneuploidy fraction over passages

c2.why: By analogy with AICAR (AMPK activator) in trisomic MEFs

c3.note: AICAR, an AMPK activator, is selectively antiproliferative in aneuploid MEFs

c4.why: Paediatric T2D experience; GI effects; B12 deficiency

c5.why: Lactic acidosis risk with reduced eGFR (nephrocalcinosis) means a kidney gate review; may worsen growth or weight in a child with failure to thrive

candidates.counter: Metformin is not AICAR, and AMPK-mediated selection is only shown for trisomies. Failure to thrive argues against an anorexigenic drug.
candidates.hypothesis: Metformin reduces the aneuploid fraction in long-term patient fibroblast culture
candidates.endpoint: Interphase FISH over passages; growth curves

c2.why: Whether cGAS-STING drives MVA pathology, and in which direction, is unknown

c3.note: MVA is linked to chronic immune response (review)

c5.why: Baricitinib/tofacitinib carry boxed malignancy warnings (ruxolitinib does not); weakens immune surveillance in a cancer-predisposed child

candidates.counter: cGAS-STING-driven immune clearance of CIN cells may be protective (28738408). Direction unknown.
candidates.hypothesis: Patient cells show an ISG signature that JAK inhibition reverses without raising aneuploid-cell survival

candidates.branch: A: block proteasomal clearance of mutant BUBR1

c1.note: MG132 blocks degradation of HSP90-destabilised MVA mutant BUBR1 in vitro

c2.why: Directly blocks the clearance route shown for analogous mutants

c4.why: Systemic proteasome inhibition is a cytotoxic chemotherapy, not suitable for chronic use

c5.why: Additive peripheral neuropathy with vincristine (RMS backbone); blocks APC/C-dependent mitotic proteolysis

c6.why: Useful only as an in vitro mechanistic probe

candidates.counter: Toxicity profile is incompatible with chronic use in a child on vincristine.
candidates.hypothesis: (Probe) Proteasome inhibition rescues BUBR1-N1002K levels, which would show M1
candidates.endpoint: BUBR1 level after MG132/bortezomib in patient cells

avoid.class: HSP90 inhibitors (e.g. pimitespib, approved in Japan)
avoid.why: Kinase-domain MVA mutant BUBR1 is HSP90-dependent; GA + CHX removed virtually all mutant protein (20516114)
Weaken the SAC or KARD phosphorylation further; aneuploid cells are sensitive to SAC inhibition over time (33505028)

avoid.class: p53 inhibition (e.g. pifithrin; no approved drug)
avoid.why: p53 is net protective against tissue decline in BubR1 progeroid mice (23602569)

Standard RMS backbone, so not avoidable. A checkpoint-weak background changes the response to mitotic arrest (19282667). The MVA RMS case was managed with reduced intensity (31184400), and genomic-instability disorders show treatment hypersensitivity (39264246). Flag for oncology dose review, not exclusion
Genomic-instability disorders may be exquisitely radiosensitive (39264246); evidence for MVA specifically is sparse
